newsitem.title: GERMANY: NCA says it sees stable ex-Germany business in 1997.
newsitem.headline: NCA says it sees stable ex-Germany business in 1997.

text.p: Nippon Cargo Airlines expects steady business development in Germany this year, its Central European manager said.
NCA regional manager Akira Todori told Reuters the airline did not expect a large increase in tonnage this year due to limited freighter capacity.
This would first change when a planned additional Europe freighter flight came into service, probably from September.
NCA carried 400,000 tonnes of German freight on its three weekly ex-Amsterdam flights last year.
A further 300,000 was flown by sister airline All Nippon Airways, for which NCA acts as Germany GSA, on its five weekly Frankfurt-Japan services.
NCA also used ANA freight capacity on other ex-Europe departures on an ad-hoc basis.
Todori said: "Business from Germany to Japan is stable. German machines will always be accepted for the (Japanese) machine market."
NCA's major European markets were the Netherlands, Germany and Italy, he added.
German freight tended to be machine parts or chemicals while Dutch cargo was mostly perishables and fashion items made up the bulk of Italian cargo.
Austria, Switzerland and eastern European countries were handled out of Frankfurt on an ad-hoc basis, Todori said.
But these countries had a lower priority since German rates were higher and thus generated better revenue, he noted.

Air cargo shipments to Japan from eastern Europe had included Bohemia glass from the Czech Republic, Hungarian goose liver pate and antiquities, he said. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
